messages:
maria: heads-up — saw a couple customer incidents where logs couldn't be correlated to traces. appears limited to requests routed via the edge proxy (eu-west). anyone seen this pattern?
anish: yep, noticed a spike in 'trace_id missing' alerts yesterday. digging but suspect header stripping in the proxy chain
tj: are these our trace ids (x-redwood-trace-id) or OTEL traceparent/header variations?
anish: most missing ones are from internal services using x-redwood-trace-id. otel-b3/tracestate looked OK in few samples
kevin: quick note: our log-ingest enrich job expects trace_id in jsonPayload.trace_id. if header is stripped, enrich fails silently and we lose link
maria: idea: either make enrich use span_id fallback or enrich at the proxy (add trace id to request body) — thoughts on where to fix with least blast radius?
tj: prefer not to touch request body. safer to normalize headers at the edge and add x-redwood-trace-id if there's traceparent. we already parse traceparent for sampling decisions
kevin: +1 for header normalization. also we should standardize field name in logs: trace_id (snake_case) across services. current mix of traceId/trace_id/TraceID is painful for ingest rules
maria: agreed. can we do a small rollout in the console to flip on "add-trace-id-header" per routing policy? would be useful so we can enable per-customer or per-region
anish: technically doable. proxy already has a transformation phase per-route. UI change is small (checkbox & audit log). need to confirm perf impact for high qps routes
sre-bot: deploy check — canary for proxy-config v3.8 scheduled at 1932105200, will run 10% traffic in eu-west for 30m
tj: also, long-term: we should enrich logs during ingestion if trace is in span export. proposal: OTEL collector adds trace_id to log records when both traces and logs share context, then exporter sends unified payloads to our ingest API
kevin: note: that requires join buffer and maybe extra memory on collector. retention and export volume will increase. need to quantify cost delta
maria: let's get numbers. Anish, can you prototype collector-side enrichment on a perf test replay and give token/ingest cost delta?
anish: will do. plan: replay 1m request trace set -> run collector with enrich and without -> measure additional bytes and CPU. expect ~0.5-1% increase in payload size if we only add one 16-byte hex string per log
tj: while we wait on numbers, we should also add a small check in log-ingest to look for alternate header names and if found, backfill trace_id to the event and emit a metric for %backfilled. that gives visibility without config flips
kevin: can we also normalize the field key on ingest? do a mapping: traceId|TraceID|trace_id -> trace_id, and emit a tag for original_key for debug
maria: yes. let's do both: header normalization in proxy (short rollout), ingest normalization + backfill metric (immediate), and collector enrichment (prototype)
anish: noted. I'll open a PR for proxy changes and attach a quick console mock for the routing policy flag. PR will reference the canary window from sre-bot
maria: awesome. assign owners: anish (proxy PR + console flag mock), kevin (ingest normalization + metrics), tj (collector prototype), maria (coordinating rollout + release notes)
kevin: ping me on PR review, will try to pair on the ingest tests
maria: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
otel-bot: OTEL collector trace-forward enrichment check completed: collector v0.56 supports record attributes injection via processors/config
sre-bot: reminder — open incidents should be quiet before canary. will hold if active incidents > 0
